title: The ORM must move from version 5.2 to 6.4 and run on MySQL before the cutover
summary: Hibernate 5.2 does not handle PostgreSQL 16, and 61 service tests fail. Upgrade to 6.4 and run it in production on MySQL for one week before the cutover.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: The order service uses Hibernate 5.2.18. Its support ended in 2018. Its newest PostgreSQL dialect targets PostgreSQL 9.5, not 16.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [TESTED] With 5.2 against staging, 61 of 1,912 service tests fail. Most failures come from identity columns and the JSON column orders.metadata. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] On a trial branch with 6.4, 14 of 1,912 tests fail. Each of the 14 failures traces to F1 or F3. [src: report.md]
  • [INFERRED] Version 6.4 changes some query results, for example the order of NULL values in sorted lists. [src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html: The upgrade changes how the service builds its queries. If the upgrade and the database move go out together, a new error has two possible causes. One week on MySQL separates the two causes.

blocks.title: Proposed action
blocks.html:
1. Upgrade to 6.4 on a branch. Fix the 14 failing tests with F1 and F3.
  2. Release on MySQL by 17 November 2026, before the peak freeze starts on 20 November.
  3. Watch the error rate for one week.

Effort: 8 days.
